newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's '97 borrowing need seen at 0-10 bln Skr.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's '97 borrowing need seen at 0-10 bln Skr.

text.p: Sweden's National Debt Office on Tuesday lowered its forecast for the central government borrowing requirement for 1997 to between zero and 10 billion crowns from an earlier forecast of 10-20 billion.
The office forecast the July borrowing requirement at 8.9 billion crowns and raised the expected need for June by 3.2 billion crowns to 9.0 billion.
The debt office said the lower year forecast was due mainly to a lower than expected borrowing requirement in May.

"There was a net surplus of 6.6 billion crowns in May (borrowing requirement of minus 6.6 billion crowns) which means that the borrowing requirement was 4.6 billion crowns less than in the earlier forecasts," the office said in a statement.
"The divergence between the forecast and the result was largely due to higher than expected revenue in the form of supplementary tax payments, provisional corporation tax and VAT."
The higher June forecast would not adversely impact the figure for 1997 as it was largely explained by the moving of a number of expenditure items into different months.
The forecast July borrowing requirement of 8.9 billion crowns was seven billion crowns lower than a year earlier.
"The lower borrowing requirement for July is largely explained by higher tax receipts," the office said.
The debt office said it planned to issue 20 billion crowns worth of Treasury bills in July and six billion crowns of bonds.
